scope: Directed security additions beyond pinned upstream parity; proposals only, no runtime/catalog registration
limitations: Absence was checked against all 1404 active AWS IDs, titles, evaluated fields and current evaluator metadata.
A source-linked service inventory is not an exhaustive assessment of every possible AWS service security feature.
CMK/VPC-only/immutable-retention requirements require declared workload policy; service default encryption or Internet-origin access alone is not a vulnerability.
All proposed formal requirement lists start empty; HackTricks thematic admission requires root review.

controls.security_value: Separate key control and auditability for archived application events
controls.predicate: For explicitly CMK-required archives, require a resolvable enabled CUSTOMER key; missing metadata remains UNKNOWN.
controls.why_distinct: Bus policy presence does not inspect archive encryption; there are no active archive checks.

controls.security_value: Customer key control over persisted schedule target inputs
controls.predicate: For explicitly CMK-required schedules require an enabled CUSTOMER key, collecting only key metadata and never Target.Input content.
controls.why_distinct: No active Scheduler checks; EventBridge bus policies do not inspect Scheduler data encryption.

controls.security_value: Enforce a declared VPC-only network perimeter on S3 access points
controls.predicate: For VPC-required access points require NetworkOrigin=VPC and the declared VPC ID; complete Internet-origin metadata fails only within that declared scope.
controls.why_distinct: Public Access Block does not restrict authenticated access to a designated VPC.
controls.customer_input: VPC-required access point scope and allowed VPCs

controls.security_value: Prevent NFS client root privilege even where mount and write access are intentionally allowed
controls.predicate: For root-restricted file systems prove an effective Deny of ClientRootAccess except declared management principals. Unsupported policy conditions remain UNKNOWN; absence of an Allow in the resource policy alone cannot prove denial because identity policies also apply.
controls.why_distinct: A named principal or access-point POSIX identity can still receive ClientRootAccess; neither existing check establishes an IAM root-access deny.
controls.customer_input: Root-restricted file system scope and management-principal exceptions

controls.security_value: Distinguish irreversible ransomware-resistant retention from a removable IAM deletion deny
controls.predicate: For immutable-retention-required vaults require Locked=true, a valid LockDate at or before capture time, and policy-compatible retention limits; a future LockDate is still changeable. Missing policy criteria remain UNKNOWN.
controls.why_distinct: A backup vault access policy remains administratively mutable; aws_log_archive_immutable concerns CloudTrail S3 destinations rather than Backup Vault Lock.
controls.customer_input: Vault immutability and retention policy; no destructive lock operation is proposed

controls.security_value: Reduce reuse of stolen long-lived refresh tokens through token rotation
controls.predicate: For supported clients with declared rotation requirement require Feature=ENABLED and the declared maximum retry grace; report configuration only, never proof that an application safely stores tokens. Omit ClientSecret from snapshots.
controls.why_distinct: Revocation capability does not enable refresh token rotation; the current client check only inspects EnableTokenRevocation.
controls.customer_input: Supported client scope, migration compatibility and retry grace policy
